## Load R packages
```{r}
# Load required packages for pathway enrichment analysis
# clusterProfiler: performs Over-Representation Analysis (ORA) and Gene Set Enrichment Analysis (GSEA)
# Reference: https://yulab-smu.top/biomedical-knowledge-mining-book/
library(clusterProfiler)

# tidyverse: data manipulation tools
library(tidyverse)

# Resolve function name conflicts between packages
library(conflicted)
conflict_prefer("select", "dplyr")  # Use dplyr's select() instead of MASS::select()
conflict_prefer("filter", "dplyr")  # Use dplyr's filter() instead of stats::filter()

# Set seed for reproducibility in permutation tests (GSEA)
set.seed(123)
```

## Import all omics
```{r}
# Import differential expression results and functional annotations
# These files contain pre-processed data from upstream analyses

# Load differential expression/abundance results across all omics
# Contains log fold changes (logFC) and FDR values for each entity (gene/protein/metabolite)
all_DE.df <- readRDS("/Users/wmujchariyak/Desktop/All_entity_fold_change_long_format.rds")

# Load functional annotation database
# Maps genes/proteins to biological pathways (GO terms, KEGG pathways, etc.)
all.annot <- readRDS("/Users/wmujchariyak/Desktop/All_funct_annot_clean_noduplicate.rda")
```

## Set parameters
```{r}
# Define thresholds and filters for enrichment analysis

# ORA (Over-Representation Analysis) specific parameters:
my_FDR <- 0.05  # False Discovery Rate threshold (5% FDR cutoff)
                # Only genes/proteins with FDR < 0.05 are considered significant
my_logFC <- 1   # Log2 fold change threshold (2-fold change)
                # Only entities with |logFC| > 1 are included

# Parameters for both ORA and GSEA:
# Use all available annotation sources (GO, KEGG, etc.)
annot_origin <- unique(all.annot$fterm_origin) %>% as.character()

# Filter for core genes (present across all strains)
# "yes" = include only core genome genes
is_core_accessory <- "yes"
```

## Example for only Transcriptomics 
### ORA & GSEA 
```{r}
# Perform pathway enrichment analysis on transcriptomics data
# This example demonstrates both ORA and GSEA approaches
# Reference: https://yulab-smu.top/biomedical-knowledge-mining-book/enrichment-overview.html

## STEP 1: Prepare Transcriptome data
my_species <- "Streptococcus pyogenes"
my_omics <- "Transcriptomics RG"

# Filter differential expression results for specified species and omics type
all_DE.res <- all_DE.df %>%
  filter(species == my_species) %>%
  filter(experiment == my_omics)

# Select appropriate annotations based on omics type
# Metabolites use different annotation schemes than genes/proteins
if (grepl("Metabo", my_omics)){
  my.annot <- all.annot %>%
    filter(entity_type == "metabolite")
} else {
  my.annot <- all.annot %>%
    filter(entity_type != "metabolite")
}

# Initialize storage lists for results from each strain
Trans.list.ORA <- list()           # Store ORA enrichment results
Trans.list.ORA.summary <- list()   # Store ORA summaries with logFC info

Trans.list.GSEA <- list()          # Store GSEA enrichment results
Trans.list.GSEA.summary <- list()  # Store GSEA summaries

# Loop through each bacterial strain for enrichment analysis
for (my_strain in unique(all_DE.res$strain)){
  
  ## PART A: Over-Representation Analysis (ORA)
  # ORA tests if significantly DE genes are over-represented in specific pathways
  # Approach: Uses a 2x2 contingency table (in pathway & DE vs not in pathway & not DE)
  # Reference: https://yulab-smu.top/biomedical-knowledge-mining-book/ora.html
  
  # Filter for significantly differentially expressed genes
  ORA.df <- all_DE.res %>%
    filter(is_species_core %in% is_core_accessory) %>%  # Core genes only
    filter(strain == my_strain) %>%                      # Current strain
    filter(FDR < my_FDR) %>%                             # Significant by FDR
    filter(abs(logFC) > my_logFC)                        # Significant fold change
  
  # Extract gene list for ORA (significantly DE genes only)
  glist.ORA <- ORA.df$entity_id
  
  # Define background gene set (all genes tested, not just significant ones)
  # Crucial for accurate statistical testing
  bglist.ORA <- all_DE.res %>%
    filter(is_species_core %in% is_core_accessory) %>%
    filter(strain == my_strain) %>%
    distinct(entity_id, .keep_all = T) %>%
    .$entity_id
  
  # Prepare term-to-gene mapping (which genes belong to which pathways)
  term_to_gene.df <- my.annot %>%
    filter(fterm_origin %in% annot_origin) %>%
    filter(entity_id %in% bglist.ORA) %>%
    dplyr::select(fterm_id, entity_id) %>%
    distinct(fterm_id, entity_id) %>%
    ungroup()
  
  # Prepare term-to-name mapping (pathway ID to pathway description)
  term_to_name.df <- my.annot %>%
    filter(fterm_origin %in% annot_origin) %>%
    filter(entity_id %in% bglist.ORA) %>%
    dplyr::select(fterm_id, fterm_name) %>%
    distinct(fterm_id, fterm_name) %>%
    ungroup()
  
  # Calculate mean/median logFC for each pathway
  # Helps interpret pathway direction (up-regulated vs down-regulated)
  ORA_logFC_summary <- ORA.df %>% 
    merge(., term_to_gene.df , by = "entity_id", all.x = T) %>%
    group_by(strain, fterm_id) %>%
    summarise(mean_logFC = mean(logFC), median_logFC = median(logFC)) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    dplyr::select(-strain)
  
  # Run Over-Representation Analysis
  # Uses hypergeometric test to identify enriched pathways
  ORA <- enricher(
    gene = glist.ORA,                       # Significantly DE genes
    TERM2GENE = term_to_gene.df,            # Pathway-to-gene mapping
    TERM2NAME = term_to_name.df,            # Pathway ID to name mapping
    universe = bglist.ORA,                  # Background gene universe
    qvalueCutoff = 1,                       # No q-value filter (keep all results)
    minGSSize = 5,                          # Minimum pathway size (≥ 5 genes)
    maxGSSize = length(bglist.ORA)/2,       # Maximum pathway size (≤ 50% of all genes)
    pvalueCutoff = 1,                       # No p-value filter (keep all results)
    pAdjustMethod = "fdr"                   # Multiple testing correction method
  )
  
  # Store ORA results
  Trans.list.ORA[[my_strain]] <- ORA
  
  # Create ORA summary with fold change information
  Trans.list.ORA.summary[[my_strain]] <- ORA %>% 
    as.data.frame() %>% 
    mutate(strain = my_strain) %>%
    mutate(experiment = my_omics) %>%
    merge(., ORA_logFC_summary, by.x = "ID", by.y = "fterm_id") 
  
  ###############
  ## PART B: Gene Set Enrichment Analysis (GSEA)
  # GSEA examines if pathway genes are enriched at the top/bottom of ranked gene list
  # Advantage over ORA: Uses all genes (not just significant ones), considers magnitude
  # Reference: https://yulab-smu.top/biomedical-knowledge-mining-book/gsea.html
  
  # Prepare gene list for GSEA (all genes, not just significant)
  GSEA.df <- all_DE.res %>%
    filter(is_species_core %in% is_core_accessory) %>%
    filter(strain == my_strain) %>%
    filter(experiment == my_omics) %>%
    distinct(entity_id, .keep_all = T) 
  
  # Create ranked gene list based on logFC
  # Higher logFC = more up-regulated in SERUM vs RPMI
  glist.GSEA <- GSEA.df$logFC 
  names(glist.GSEA) <- GSEA.df$entity_id
  
  # Sort in descending order (most up-regulated first)
  # GSEA uses this ranking to determine if pathway genes cluster at extremes
  glist.GSEA <- sort(glist.GSEA, decreasing = T)
  
  # Run Gene Set Enrichment Analysis
  # Uses Kolmogorov-Smirnov-like statistic to detect pathway enrichment
  GSEA <- GSEA(
    geneList = glist.GSEA,                  # Ranked gene list (all genes)
    TERM2GENE = term_to_gene.df,            # Pathway-to-gene mapping
    TERM2NAME = term_to_name.df,            # Pathway ID to name mapping
    minGSSize = 5,                          # Minimum pathway size
    maxGSSize = length(bglist.ORA)/2,       # Maximum pathway size
    maxGSSize = length(bglist.ORA)/2,       # Maximum pathway size
    pvalueCutoff = 1,                       # No p-value filter (keep all)
    pAdjustMethod = "fdr",                  # FDR correction
    nPermSimple = 100000,                   # Number of permutations (high for precision)
    eps = 0                                 # Allow p-values < 1/nPermSimple
  )
  
  # Store GSEA results
  Trans.list.GSEA[[my_strain]] <- GSEA
  
  # Create GSEA summary with pathway names
  Trans.list.GSEA.summary[[my_strain]] <- GSEA %>% 
    as.data.frame() %>% 
    mutate(strain = my_strain) %>%
    mutate(experiment = my_omics) %>%
    merge(., term_to_name.df, by.x = "ID", by.y = "fterm_id", all.x = T) 
}

# Key differences between ORA and GSEA:
# ORA: Uses only significant genes, tests over-representation
# GSEA: Uses all genes ranked by expression, detects coordinated changes
# Both methods are complementary and provide different insights
```

### Check ORA and GSEA Results
```{r}
# Examine enrichment results for a representative strain
# View top 5 enriched pathways from ORA
head(Trans.list.ORA.summary[["5448"]], 5)

# View top 5 enriched pathways from GSEA
head(Trans.list.GSEA.summary[["5448"]], 5)

# Interpretation tips:
# - p.adjust < 0.05: significantly enriched pathway
# - GeneRatio: proportion of DE genes in the pathway
# - BgRatio: proportion of background genes in the pathway
# - NES (GSEA): normalized enrichment score (positive = up, negative = down)
```


## For loop - ORA & GSEA analysis (All omics and all strains)
```{r}
# List of omics experiments
omics_list <- c("Transcriptomics RG", "Proteomics MS1 DDA", "Metabolomics GC-MS")

# Initialize lists to store results
results_list <- list()

# Loop through omics types
for (my_omics in omics_list) {
  
  cat("\nProcessing Omics Experiment:", my_omics, "\n")
  
  # Prepare data for the current omics
  my_species <- "Streptococcus pyogenes"
  
  all_DE.res <- all_DE.df %>%
    filter(species == my_species) %>%
    filter(experiment == my_omics)
  
  # Filter annotation based on metabolite or non-metabolite
  if (grepl("Metabo", my_omics)) {
    my.annot <- all.annot %>%
      filter(entity_type == "metabolite")
  } else {
    my.annot <- all.annot %>%
      filter(entity_type != "metabolite")
  }
  
  # Initialize lists for ORA and GSEA results
  omics_list_ORA <- list()
  omics_list_ORA_summary <- list()
  
  omics_list_GSEA <- list()
  omics_list_GSEA_summary <- list()
  
  # Iterate over strains within the current omics experiment
  for (my_strain in unique(all_DE.res$strain)) {
    
    # ORA Analysis
    ORA.df <- all_DE.res %>%
      filter(is_species_core %in% is_core_accessory) %>%
      filter(strain == my_strain) %>%
      filter(FDR < my_FDR) %>%
      filter(abs(logFC) > my_logFC)
    
    glist.ORA <- ORA.df$entity_id
    
    # Background gene list
    bglist.ORA <- all_DE.res %>%
      filter(is_species_core %in% is_core_accessory) %>%
      filter(strain == my_strain) %>%
      distinct(entity_id, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
      .$entity_id
    
    # Prepare term-to-gene and term-to-name mappings
    term_to_gene.df <- my.annot %>%
      filter(fterm_origin %in% annot_origin) %>%
      filter(entity_id %in% bglist.ORA) %>%
      dplyr::select(fterm_id, entity_id) %>%
      distinct(fterm_id, entity_id) %>%
      ungroup()
    
    term_to_name.df <- my.annot %>%
      filter(fterm_origin %in% annot_origin) %>%
      filter(entity_id %in% bglist.ORA) %>%
      dplyr::select(fterm_id, fterm_name) %>%
      distinct(fterm_id, fterm_name) %>%
      ungroup()
    
    # Calculate summary statistics for ORA
    ORA_logFC_summary <- ORA.df %>%
      merge(., term_to_gene.df, by = "entity_id", all.x = TRUE) %>%
      group_by(strain, fterm_id) %>%
      summarise(mean_logFC = mean(logFC), median_logFC = median(logFC)) %>%
      ungroup() %>%
      dplyr::select(-strain)
    
    # Perform ORA
    ORA <- enricher(
      gene = glist.ORA,
      TERM2GENE = term_to_gene.df,
      TERM2NAME = term_to_name.df,
      universe = bglist.ORA,
      qvalueCutoff = 1,
      minGSSize = 5,
      maxGSSize = length(bglist.ORA) / 2,
      pvalueCutoff = 1,
      pAdjustMethod = "fdr"
    )
    
    # Store ORA results
    omics_list_ORA[[my_strain]] <- ORA
    omics_list_ORA_summary[[my_strain]] <- ORA %>%
      as.data.frame() %>%
      mutate(strain = my_strain) %>%
      mutate(experiment = my_omics) %>%
      merge(., ORA_logFC_summary, by.x = "ID", by.y = "fterm_id")
    
    # GSEA Analysis
    GSEA.df <- all_DE.res %>%
      filter(is_species_core %in% is_core_accessory) %>%
      filter(strain == my_strain) %>%
      filter(experiment == my_omics) %>%
      distinct(entity_id, .keep_all = TRUE)
    
    glist.GSEA <- GSEA.df$logFC
    names(glist.GSEA) <- GSEA.df$entity_id
    glist.GSEA <- sort(glist.GSEA, decreasing = TRUE)
    
    GSEA <- GSEA(
      geneList = glist.GSEA,
      TERM2GENE = term_to_gene.df,
      TERM2NAME = term_to_name.df,
      minGSSize = 5,
      maxGSSize = length(bglist.ORA) / 2,
      pvalueCutoff = 1,
      pAdjustMethod = "fdr",
      nPermSimple = 100000,  # Increase the number of permutations
      eps = 0  # Allow more precise p-value estimation
    )
    
    # Store GSEA results
    omics_list_GSEA[[my_strain]] <- GSEA
    omics_list_GSEA_summary[[my_strain]] <- GSEA %>%
      as.data.frame() %>%
      mutate(strain = my_strain) %>%
      mutate(experiment = my_omics) %>%
      merge(., term_to_name.df, by.x = "ID", by.y = "fterm_id", all.x = TRUE)
  }
  
  # Save all results for this omics
  results_list[[my_omics]] <- list(
    ORA = omics_list_ORA,
    ORA_summary = omics_list_ORA_summary,
    GSEA = omics_list_GSEA,
    GSEA_summary = omics_list_GSEA_summary
  )
}
```
